title: C'est la femme des impôts?  (Is That the Tax Woman?)

segments.t: Meanwhile in Paris, Andréa wakes up in her apartment with Colette Brancillon, the tax inspector auditing ASK. As they leave the building together, a frantic Gabriel intercepts Andréa on the pavement — and recognizes Colette. Listen to the scene in French first; don't worry about catching every word.
Viens là.
Je vais prendre une douche.
Voilà. De rien!
Je vais vraiment être en retard.
Moi aussi.
Tu étais où? Tu ne répondais pas au téléphone.
Il y a eu un drame sur le tournage!
Désolée. J'étais avec une fille.
Tu aurais quand même pu répondre.
C'est la femme des impôts?
Non.
Incroyable! Et si c'est ta voisine?
C'est effrayant!
Tu me manques déjà.
Let's go back through it step by step. It is morning in Andréa's bedroom, and she reaches out for Colette before they both have to leave for work.
Viens là.
'Come here.' The casual command of 'to come', followed by the word for 'there' or 'here'.
Je vais prendre une douche.
'I'm going to take a shower.' The near future built with 'I go' plus the infinitive 'to take'.
Voilà. De rien!
'There you go. You're welcome!' In the kitchen, Colette hands Andréa a fresh slice of toast after she drops hers on the floor. Literally 'of nothing'.
Je vais vraiment être en retard.
'I'm really going to be late.' Notice how the adverb 'really' sits right between 'I am going' and 'to be'.
Moi aussi.
'Me too.' The stressed pronoun for 'me' with the word for 'also'.
Tu étais où? Tu ne répondais pas au téléphone.
'Where were you? You weren't answering your phone.' Outside on the street, Gabriel rushes up to Andréa using the imperfect past tense for what was happening.
Il y a eu un drame sur le tournage!
'There was a crisis on the film shoot!' The past tense of 'there is', literally 'it has had a drama on the shoot'.
Désolée. J'étais avec une fille.
'Sorry. I was with a girl.' Andréa explains why her phone was off without mentioning who the woman was.
Tu aurais quand même pu répondre.
'You still could have answered.' Literally 'you would all the same have been able to answer'.
C'est la femme des impôts?
'Is that the tax woman?' Gabriel spots Colette walking down the pavement after leaving Andréa's building.
Non.
'No.' Not wanting Gabriel to know she spent the night with the auditor, Andréa lies without blinking.
Incroyable! Et si c'est ta voisine?
'Incredible! What if she's your neighbour?' Gabriel assumes Colette must live in the same building.
C'est effrayant!
'That's scary!' Gabriel shudders at the thought of living next door to the tax inspector.
Tu me manques déjà.

'I miss you already.' In the taxi, Andréa's phone buzzes with a sweet message from Colette. In French, the person you miss is the subject: literally 'you are lacking to me already'. Now let's hear the whole scene with Andréa, Colette, and Gabriel again.
Viens là.
Je vais prendre une douche.
Voilà. De rien!
Je vais vraiment être en retard.
Moi aussi.
Tu étais où? Tu ne répondais pas au téléphone.
Il y a eu un drame sur le tournage!
Désolée. J'étais avec une fille.
Tu aurais quand même pu répondre.
C'est la femme des impôts?
Non.
Incroyable! Et si c'est ta voisine?
C'est effrayant!
Tu me manques déjà.
While Andréa hides her new romance with the tax inspector from Gabriel and they head out to the country film set, back in Paris it is Camille's twenty-third birthday. See you next time.
Bonne soirée!
